requirement:
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
rationale:
The tests cover every obligation of `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`. Bedrock is the only backend with explicit checkpoints, so it is the only one the first paragraph applies to. The other three obligations are covered as follows.

- **Two checkpoints per request on a caching model.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage]` runs a Claude model. For both requests it asserts that `system` is the prompt followed by one `cachePoint`. It asserts that the last message's content ends with a `cachePoint`. It asserts that the whole body has exactly two `cachePoint` occurrences. The second request follows a reasoning turn and a tool result, and it still ends in a checkpoint. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models]` checks the model gate `bedrock_caches` for Claude, Nova, Llama and the fixture model. It also checks that `place_cache_checkpoints` sets the cache option, including after a reasoning turn.
- **Checkpoints do not change content.** The Claude test runs the same conversation on a non-caching model. It asserts that the cached bodies equal the plain bodies once `without_cache_points` strips the checkpoints. It also asserts that the plain request has no `cachePoint`. The providers unit test compares the serialized request with the same request that differs only in the cache option.
- **Model refuses a checkpoint.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_continues_when_the_model_refuses_a_checkpoint_after_reasoning]` covers Nova and an unlisted Claude model. It asserts that the follow-up request keeps the same system block and has no checkpoint in its messages. It also asserts that the reasoning and tool-result messages are present.
- **OpenAI.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` asserts that `instructions` and `tools` are identical across the two requests. It asserts that the second request's `input` begins with the first request's `input` unchanged. It asserts that the function call and its output follow in order. It calls `assert_no_checkpoints` on every request body.

I found no uncovered obligation and no marking gap.

text: :::{req} cache_checkpoints
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.
For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
:::{req} prompt_parts
Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
test-adequacy requirement, structural requirement, example, citation review, site
review. A system prompt MUST be the same for
every assessment of its kind, so every placeholder whose value depends on the
subject MUST be in the subject message.
